stem: Identify the particles whose attraction forms metallic bonding.

options.A: Neutral metal atoms and shared pairs of electrons
options.B: Positive metal ions and delocalised electrons
options.C: Positive metal ions and negative metal ions
options.D: Positive nuclei and localised bonding pairs

stem: Identify the correct description of electrons in a metallic lattice.

options.A: Electrons form negative ions at lattice sites
options.B: Each electron belongs to a fixed pair of atoms
options.C: Electrons are delocalised throughout the lattice
options.D: Electrons stay inside neutral metal atoms

stem:
Copper has a high melting point.
What is the reason for the high melting point of copper?

options.A: strong attractive forces between copper atoms only
options.B: strong attractive forces between copper ions and delocalised electrons
options.C: strong attractive forces between copper ions only
options.D: strong attractive forces between copper atoms and delocalised electrons

stem:
Which statements help to explain the increase in melting point from sodium to aluminium?
1
The charge on the metal ion increases.
2
There are more delocalised electrons per metal ion.
3
The radius of the metal ion decreases.
Which statement explains why sodium and potassium have different melting points?

options.A: The attraction between cations and delocalised electrons is stronger in sodium.
options.B: The attraction between cations and anions is stronger in sodium.
options.C: The attraction between atoms is stronger in sodium.
options.D: The attraction between nuclei and shared electron pairs is stronger in sodium.

stem: Which pair of particles attracts in metallic bonding?

options.A: Positive metal ions and delocalised electrons
options.C: Neutral atoms and fixed shared pairs
